text:
Jack Hughes has spent most of November as the guy setting the table, and Friday he finally ate. One goal and three assists against Calgary, including the breakaway that tied it 3-3 and the setup on the winner, in a comeback the Devils needed.

That night also nudged a number that has looked wrong all season. Hughes has 11 goals on 13.8 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and before Friday he had one goal in nine games while still putting five shots on net some nights. The looks are there, and goals tend to follow looks. Everything else is humming: 34 points in 26 games, and with him on the ice at five on five the Devils get 63% of the expected goals, which is elite territory.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 97th percentile last season for chances from the slot, and he carries the puck in more than he dumps it. Our range has him finishing somewhere between 91 and 119 points. The thing to watch is the shooting: if it catches up to the chances, the top of that range is in play.
